meaning:
ἀπο-καθ-ίστημι (ἀποκαθιστάω, Mrk.9:12, Rec., -ιστάνω, LTTr.; cf. Act.1:6; -κατιστάνω, WH),
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ;]
1. to restore, i.e. to a former condition: of health, Mat.12:13, Mrk.3:5 8:25, Luk.6:10; of social or political affairs, Mat.17:11, Mrk.9:12, Act.1:6.
2. to give back, bring back: Heb.13:19 (so in π., MM, see word; cf. also Cremer, 312).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out; and it was restored whole, just like the other.
When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out…
He looked around at them all, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.
Therefore when they had come together, they asked him, “Lord, are you now restoring the kingdom to Israel?”
I strongly urge you to do this, that I may be restored to you sooner.
